learning_objective: 🎯 Take the derivative out of the textbook and use it to solve real-world problems like maximizing profit, finding speed, and calculating errors!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Derivatives show how fast one thing is changing compared to another. For example, how fast the area of a circle grows as its radius increases. It’s like a mathematical speedometer.
If the first derivative ($dy/dx$) is positive, the graph is going uphill (increasing). If it is negative, the graph is going downhill (decreasing).
This is about finding the highest peak (maxima) or lowest valley (minima) of a curve. You find these by seeing where the slope becomes completely flat (derivative equals zero).
Once you find a flat point, you take the second derivative to test it. If the second derivative is positive, it's a valley (Minima). If it's negative, it's a peak (Maxima)!

fun_activity.title: 📦 The Perfect Box Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Take a square piece of cardboard. If you cut small squares from the corners and fold up the sides, you get a box. Use derivatives to calculate exactly what size squares you should cut to hold the MAXIMUM amount of volume!

exam_tips: 📌 When finding Absolute Maxima/Minima on a closed interval [a, b], NEVER forget to test the exact endpoints 'a' and 'b' along with your critical points.
📌 Be careful with units in 'Rate of Change' word problems (e.g., $cm^3/sec$). Writing the final answer without units will cost you half a mark.
📌 In word problems for Maxima/Minima, carefully identify the 'Given' (constant) and the 'To Maximize/Minimize' (function) to set up your equation properly.
quick_recap: ⭐ Critical points occur where the first derivative is zero or undefined.
⭐ The Second Derivative test helps confirm if a point is a local maximum or minimum.
